## Findings
1. On 17 April 2025, Calder Freight Services Ltd delivered a consignment of chilled goods to Eastwick Central Depot at a recorded core temperature of 9.4℃, exceeding the agreed limit of 5.0℃. This caused stock worth £1,500 to be destroyed, contrary to clause 9(1)(b) of the Chilled Goods Supply Agreement 2019 {cite:supplier-review-calder.pdf#3,5,7,8,14}.
2. On 13 May 2025, at Prior Lane Warehouse, the supplier's driver unloaded a consignment without obtaining the required second signature. A crate of laboratory glassware worth £600 was later found to be missing, contrary to clause 12(2) of the Chilled Goods Supply Agreement 2019 {cite:supplier-review-calder.pdf#3,5,7,8,14}.
3. On 5 May 2025, at Forest Yard, a trailer was left unsecured overnight, resulting in the loss of a pallet of archive boxes worth £2,049, contrary to clause 7(1) of the Chilled Goods Supply Agreement 2019 {cite:supplier-review-calder.pdf#3,5,7,8,14}.

## Supplier's Response
Calder Freight Services Ltd admitted findings 1 and 6 but disputed finding 4, claiming that depot staff had waved the driver through. The supplier submitted its written response on 2 June 2025 {cite:supplier-review-calder.pdf#5,7,8}.

## Losses Claimed
The total losses claimed amount to £4,149, broken down as follows:
- £1,500 for chilled stock destroyed at Eastwick Central Depot.
- £600 for missing laboratory glassware at Prior Lane Warehouse.
- £2,049 for lost archive boxes at Forest Yard {cite:supplier-review-calder.pdf#5,7,8}.

## Compliance History
Calder Freight Services Ltd has a history of breaches, including:
- Six late delivery breaches (2015–2024).
- Three temperature control breaches (2017–2023).
- Two record-keeping breaches (2016–2019).
- One security breach (2021) {cite:supplier-review-calder.pdf#3,14}.

## Proposed Outcome
The reviewer has proposed a six-month probation period for Calder Freight Services Ltd, with monthly temperature audits. The matter is scheduled for the review panel on 15 July 2025 {cite:supplier-review-calder.pdf#5,7,8}.
